subject: SLA addendum request: on‑prem heartbeat detection & evidence window
messages:
From: Eva Martinez <ops+contracts@thermalion.com>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SLA addendum for on‑prem heartbeat & evidence window

Hi Nikhil,

Quick background: Thermalion is moving a subset of production traffic to a private VPC where we control the peering and edge routers. Over the last two months we've observed intermittent packet loss that correlates with maintenance windows on our transit provider. Those incidents look like customer‑side network interruptions, but our legal/ops teams need an explicit SLA appendix so we can proceed with Redwood in a compliance review.

Specifically we are asking for three items:
- An availability carveout that excludes customer‑controlled network interruptions when we can show traces/heartbeats;
- Defined "Operational Evidence Window" — the period during which telemetry and logs are preserved for dispute adjudication (we'd prefer 30 days);
- A list of the artifacts Redwood will accept as evidence (heartbeat traces, KV cache timestamps, server‑side request IDs).

Can Redwood provide a short addendum we can take to procurement? We're trying to finalize procurement by May 1.

Thanks,
Eva Martinez
Director, Platform
Thermalion Labs

Attachments: none
From: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
To: Eva Martinez <ops+contracts@thermalion.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SLA addendum for on‑prem heartbeat & evidence window

Eva — thanks for the clear summary. We can accommodate an addendum, but there are a few tradeoffs we need to align on up front so the language is implementable and operationally testable.

High level proposal (options):
1) Evidence window: Redwood can commit to retaining server telemetry that pertains to private deployments for 45 days by default (we can compress/aggregate older data). If Thermalion requires 30 days instead, we can accept that as long as you confirm retention on your side for network traces.
2) Availability split: For private/VPC deployments we typically operate to a composite SLO where Redwood is responsible for the inference runtime and customer is responsible for customer‑controlled networking. We can add explicit language that customer‑side network interruptions are excluded from Redwood uptime calculations when Thermalion provides the agreed evidence set.
3) Evidence set: we accept the following as primary artifacts: Redwood request IDs & timestamps, KV cache hit logs (sampled), server heartbeats (per minute summary), and traceroute / tcpdump captures from the customer side showing path instability.

Next steps: I'll loop in Legal and our PM on telemetry retention and draft a short addendum. Kim/Naomi — can you weigh in on the credit cap language (we typically cap credits for private deployments) and the operational evidence window?

— Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Eva Martinez <ops+contracts@thermalion.com>, nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: SLA addendum for on‑prem heartbeat & evidence window

Hi Eva / team — thanks for the request and Nikhil for the draft options. From a contractual standpoint we propose the following concrete items that map to Redwood's operational capabilities: 

1) Operational Evidence Window: Redwood will retain inference runtime telemetry relevant to private/VPC deployments for a period of 45 days. Redwood will make production request/heartbeat logs available to the customer on request within that period.
2) Evidence artifacts: accepted evidence will include (a) Redwood request IDs and per‑request latency traces, (b) KV cache timestamps and hit rates (sampled), (c) server heartbeat aggregates, and (d) customer‑provided traceroute/tcpdump showing network anomalies temporally aligned to Redwood request IDs.
3) Credit cap & liability: For private deployments, any service credits related to availability reductions attributable to Redwood (after evidence review) will be capped at the lesser of (i) 10% of the affected month’s invoice or (ii) $75,000 per incident. Credits will not apply to interruptions attributable to customer‑controlled network or misconfigurations.
4) Operational preconditions: Proof of correct peering configuration (BGP session up, NAT mapping for egress, firewall rules allowing our health probes) is required prior to final promulgation. If the customer cannot produce the requested traces during an incident, Redwood reserves the right to treat the incident as inconclusive.

I've attached a short draft addendum (thermalion‑sla‑addendum‑draft.docx) that reflects the above. We can take Thermalion's redlines and iterate. Please note Redwood's retention commitments are constrained by our storage and privacy policy; 45 days is the default for private deployments. If Thermalion insists on a shorter window we can consider a 30‑day special arrangement in exchange for a telemetry retention surcharge.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: thermalion-sla-addendum-draft.docx (docx)
From: Eva Martinez <ops+contracts@thermalion.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SLA addendum for on‑prem heartbeat & evidence window

Kim / Nikhil — thanks for the clear options and the draft. We reviewed internally and can accept Redwood's proposed language with two small edits:

1) Thermalion requests the Operational Evidence Window be 30 days (we commit to retaining our network traces for 60 days and to provide them promptly).
2) Add a short runbook commitment: Redwood will acknowledge evidence submission within 72 hours and provide an initial determination whether the incident appears customer‑side vs. provider‑side within 7 business days. Final credit adjudication can take longer but we need the initial disposition for procurement.

I've attached our redline (thermalion-signed-redline.pdf). If Redwood can accept those two edits we're ready to sign and move to procurement.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this week.
Eva Martinez
Director, Platform
Thermalion Labs
